alerts.summary: ## Summary An unauthenticated (**Anonymous**) client can **Write** protected Variables and **Call** privileged Methods on any Node that lacks explicit per-node permissions. This follows the inheritance model defined by OPC UA Part 3, §5.2.9, where nodes without an explicit `RolePermissions` attribute inherit the namespace `DefaultRolePermissions`. OPC 10000-3 §4.8.3 mandates a **default-deny** evaluation (`Bad_UserAccessDenied` when the operation bits are not set); `node-opcua` instead **grants all permissions**. The root cause is a combination of an authorization **fail-open** and a **disconnect** between the configuration API and the runtime enforcement path. --- ## Affected configuration This advisory covers two cases that are not equally severe: 1. No RolePermissions declared anywhere - resolution is permissive. This is node-opcua's documented behaviour for a server with no access co
alerts.title: node-opcua: Namespace-Level RBAC Fail-Open - Anonymous Write/Call Bypass via Unbound `DefaultRolePermissions

alerts.summary: ### Summary The `POST /__nuxt_content/:collection/query` endpoint in `@nuxt/content` accepts an attacker-controlled `sql` field from the HTTP request body and executes it against a local SQLite database after passing it through an insufficient validator (`assertSafeQuery`). The validator only blocks a small set of SQL command keywords and does not reject expensive SQLite built-in functions such as `randomblob()`, `zeroblob()`, `hex()`, or `length()`. An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a single request that forces SQLite to allocate hundreds of megabytes of memory and perform CPU-intensive work, causing server-wide denial of service. This endpoint is enabled by default for every collection and requires no authentication. ### Details The vulnerability spans three source files: **Route registration — `src/module.ts:207-208`** The Nuxt Content module registers a public HTTP POST ha
alerts.title: Nuxt Content: Unauthenticated SQLite Function DoS via Content Query API

alerts.summary: ### Impact An authenticated non-administrative user could access a Kubernetes cluster they are not authorized to access through GPUStack's Kubernetes API proxy. The `cluster_apiserver_proxy` handler did not perform a resource-level authorization check before forwarding requests to the selected cluster. Requests were forwarded through a worker using its Kubernetes ServiceAccount credentials. Depending on the permissions granted to that ServiceAccount, an attacker could read sensitive Kubernetes resources, create or modify workloads, or delete resources and disrupt services. Creating attacker-controlled workloads could result in code execution in the target cluster. Exploitation requires a Kubernetes-provider cluster with a reachable worker. The operations available to the attacker are limited by the worker's ServiceAccount permissions. ### Patches Fixed in `gpustack` `v2.2.2`. ### Workaro
alerts.title: GPUStack: Missing authorization on several cluster and resource endpoints allows cross-user access and cluster takeover

alerts.summary: ### Summary RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 signature verification (`publicKey.verify()` with the default scheme, also used by X.509 certificate and PKCS#7 verification) accepted non-canonical BER encodings of the DigestInfo, such as NULL parameters with content and non-minimal lengths. These leave attacker-controlled bytes inside an accepted DigestInfo, which allows signatures to be forged without the private key for RSA keys with a low public exponent (e=3). Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. ### Details In `lib/rsa.js`, `key.verify()` with the default `RSASSA-PKCS1-V1_5` scheme removes the padding, parses the recovered DigestInfo with the lenient BER parser `asn1.fromDer()` and checks its structure with `asn1.validate()` against `digestInfoValidator`. Neither requires a canonical DER encoding, so verification accepted, among others: - NULL parameters with content bytes (e.g. `05 40 <64 bytes>`) - non-NULL
alerts.title: Forge: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature forgery via non-canonical DigestInfo encoding

alerts.summary: ### Summary `asn1.fromDer()` decodes the contents of BIT STRINGs as ASN.1 by default. That decode ignored the `maxDepth` recursion limit (an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-66031) and also decoded nested BIT STRINGs, keeping a full copy of the decoded contents at each level, so small crafted DER or PEM inputs (certificates, keys, PKCS structures) use excessive CPU time and memory and can abort the Node.js process. Fixed in node-forge 1.4.1. ### Details `asn1.fromDer()` attempts by default to decode the contents of primitive BIT STRINGs as ASN.1 (`decodeBitStrings`, default `true`). Two flaws in that decode in `lib/asn1.js` allow resource exhaustion: 1. `_fromDer()` started the BIT STRING decode with a new options object, `{strict: true, decodeBitStrings: true}`, that did not include `maxDepth`. Inside that decode the depth check compared against `undefined` and never triggered, so the recursi
alerts.title: Forge: ASN.1 resource exhaustion via BIT STRING decoding in asn1.fromDer

alerts.summary: ### Summary An XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) vulnerability occurs when an attacker is able to inject their own JavaScript code into a web page's source, which is subsequently processed by the victim's browser. A common cause of this vulnerability is the failure to validate user-supplied data before displaying it within the vulnerable application without proper filtering. To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker must input HTML code into a vulnerable parameter containing structures that trigger the execution of JavaScript. The DOM XSS variant occurs when user-supplied data is processed by a client-side script; if this data is not handled correctly by the script itself, it becomes possible to inject additional JavaScript commands. **Attacker model:** Any actor who can get a DICOM object in front of a victim — email a `.dcm` for local viewing, upload to a shared PACS, or operate/compromise a

alerts.summary: ### Summary The second stage pilot (pilot.tar) is downloaded by the initial wrapper script without any verification of the webservers' SSL certificate and the contained script is subsequently executed. The checksum is tested, but the reference checksum file is downloaded over the same unvalidated channel. ### Details The pilot wrapper downloads and executes the main second stage pilot script, but the SSL validation on this connection is explicitly disabled (to match old python < 2.7.9 behaviour): https://github.com/DIRACGrid/DIRAC/blob/integration/src/DIRAC/WorkloadManagementSystem/Utilities/PilotWrapper.py#L292-L296 This means that the second stage pilot code is not verified in any way and could potentially be altered by a man-in-the-middle attack to execute arbitrary code in the pilot context (i.e. with access to the pilot proxy/credentials). The HTTPS connection should be validated ag
alerts.title: DIRAC: Pilot code downloaded over unverified HTTPS connection

alerts.summary: ### Impact `sanitizeFilter` is Mongoose's mechanism for protecting against query selector injection attacks. In older versions of Mongoose, `sanitizeFilter` was not applied for `countDocuments()` queries. ### Patches Patches have been released for all supported Mongoose major release lines. Please upgrade to the following versions depending on which major version of Mongoose applications are using. 1. `^9.9.2` 2. `^8.24.3` 3. `^7.8.12` 4. `^6.13.11` ### Workarounds Middleware: ```javascript mongoose.plugin(function() { schema.pre('countDocuments', function() { // This will always apply `sanitizeFilter` on `countDocuments` mongoose.sanitizeFilter(this.getFilter()); }); }); ```
alerts.title: Mongoose: sanitizeFilter not applied on countDocuments

alerts.summary: ### Summary sanitizeFilter exists to stop query selector injection: it wraps operator objects such as `{ $ne: null }` in filter values in `$eq`, so they are matched literally. Set on a connection with `mongoose.connect()` or `createConnection(uri, { sanitizeFilter: true })`, the connection reports it as enabled but queries never apply it. An application that relies on the connection-level option and passes an attacker-controlled object into a filter therefore remains open to selector injection, and a password value of `{ $ne: null }` returns the account record without the password. ### Details `NativeConnection#createClient()` at `lib/drivers/node-mongodb-native/connection.js:270-272` moves `options.sanitizeFilter` into `Connection.config` and deletes the original option. `Query#_castConditions()` at `lib/query.js:2413-2423` checks `Connection.options`, the global `options`, and the per-
alerts.title: Mongoose: Connection-level sanitizeFilter not applied

alerts.summary: ### Summary Three Mongoose code paths copy data into objects by property name without checking whether the property is the object's own or inherited from its prototype: 1. Loading a document from the database (`init()`, also used by `Model.hydrate()`) 2. Setting a dotted path on a document (`$__set`, used by `new Model(obj)`, `doc.set()` and `doc.$set()`) 3. Merging update documents (`utils.mergeClone`, used by `findOneAndReplace()`, chained update calls and `Query.prototype.merge()`) When a key names an inherited property, such as `toString` or `valueOf`, or a document internal such as `$__schema`, Mongoose writes into the shared object behind that property. The data comes from the attacker. - **Denial of service.** For example, `{ "toString": { "call": 1 } }` overwrites `Object.prototype.toString.call`. Mongoose and most other libraries rely on `Object.prototype.toString.call()`. After
alerts.title: Mongoose walks into inherited properties when hydrating, setting, and merging, allowing overwrites of built-in functions (denial of service) and shared schema state

alerts.summary: ### Impact Crafted payloads targeting frameworks supporting React Server Components can lead to remote code execution. This only affects extremely rare cases where responses transport multiple typed arrays and an attacker-controlled value. Updating immediately is recommended. The vulnerability exists in versions 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8 and 19.3.0 of: - react-server-dom-webpack - react-server-dom-parcel - react-server-dom-turbopack ### Patches Fixes were back ported to versions 19.0.09, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1. If applications are using any of the above packages please upgrade to any of the fixed versions immediately. If an app’s React code does not use a server, the app is not affected by this vulnerability. If an app does not use a framework, bundler, or bundler plugin that supports React Server Components, the app is not affected by this
alerts.title: React: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in React Server Components
